summary: Observation of the movement of luminous shapes through the clouds.
description: On December 11, 2007, at approximately 8:40 PM, two witnesses observed lights in the cloudy sky over Toulouse. One of the witnesses reported observing, for 25 minutes, the rapid movement of slightly oval, white, and opaque shapes that created various geometric patterns through the clouds. He filmed his observation for a few minutes with his cell phone. No unusual noises were heard during the observation. The police reviewed the video taken by this witness and did indeed distinguish some movement (see police report). Based on the witness's description and after ruling out an astronomical error, it is likely that these individuals observed a light show (given the significant duration of the phenomenon). This type of moving light on cloudy surfaces is frequently misinterpreted, and depending on weather conditions, the beams may not be visible. Therefore, it is difficult to easily locate the source, which could be close to the observation area or much farther away, depending on the range of the spotlights.

summary: Spots on a series of photos taken in burst mode: mist.
description: An amateur photographer discovered unexpected objects in his burst photos taken during a weekend in Biarritz. This case is a retrospective observation of strange objects in a photograph, even though nothing was visually apparent. It's a typical example of a small object passing very close to the camera. In this instance, sea spray caused these fleeting glimpses. It's possible that birds are also visible in the distance.

summary: Observation of 3 bright points in a triangle. Witnesses reported feeling unwell
description: On November 26, 2007, between 6:20 PM and 6:35 PM, a witness was driving home with her son. She observed three bright yellow points in a triangle in the sky, with a red light in the center. The altitude appeared low, and the phenomenon was stationary. A rumbling sound was heard by the witnesses. The driver slowed down to observe the phenomenon, and her son opened the window and leaned his head out for a better view. He was then seized by intense headaches and a nervous breakdown, which greatly frightened the mother. The investigation established the precise positioning of the witnesses' vehicle at 46°46'39"N and 1°13'48"W, as well as the direction of the observation: NNE. The sighting occurred at an unspecified time between 6:20 PM and 6:35 PM local time. All aircraft movements over Nantes and La Roche-sur-Yon between 6:00 PM and 7:00 PM were reconstructed with the efficient assistance of the DGAC (French Civil Aviation Authority) services in Nantes. Seven aircraft were identified flying at a sufficiently low altitude to be clearly distinguishable from the ground (below FL020). The GEIPAN investigation has established beyond any doubt that the observation made by witnesses was of flight LXPRG at 6:27:16 PM (local time) approaching La Roche-sur-Yon airport. Since the medical analysis yielded no results, it is likely that the effects related to the stress of an unexplained sighting must be investigated. The child's earache may have been triggered by the child's poor posture while putting his head out of the moving car window, with fear and stress from the mother, already worried about her other younger son being home alone, taking their toll.

summary: probable observation of atmospheric reentry
description: On October 2, 2007, at midnight, a witness was surprised to see a red light moving horizontally across the sky at very high speed. The observation lasted a few seconds without any sound being heard. The description and duration of the observation support the hypothesis of a probable atmospheric reentry.

summary: observation of atmospheric reentry
description: On November 1, 2007, while closing his shutters at 8:34 PM, a witness observed a curious luminous phenomenon in the sky. For two to three seconds, he saw something resembling a shooting star or a white firework rocket moving at high speed across the sky at low altitude in a northeast-northwest direction. No further information was gathered. This witness reported observing the atmospheric reentry of a meteorite or space debris, although it was not possible to identify it with certainty.

summary: Yellow light falling vertically from the sky: probable observation of a bolide.
description: A witness reports that in March 2007 (between November 22nd and 28th, he doesn't remember the exact date), he made a peculiar observation. Driving on a departmental road between 8 and 10 pm, he and his passenger suddenly saw a luminous phenomenon in the middle of the sky that seemed to "dive towards the ground." The observation, which lasted 1 to 2 seconds, allowed them to distinguish a yellow, teardrop-shaped light that moved silently. The object quickly disappeared over the horizon. Based on the description given of the phenomenon (trajectory, duration), these people witnessed the reentry of a bolide into the atmosphere. The "teardrop" shape is certainly due to the presence of a wake trail following the object.

summary: Very short observation of the rapid passage towards the Northeast of a luminous phenomenon with a trail: lack of reliable information.
description: On October 27, 2007, at 11:00 PM, a motorist observed a luminous phenomenon rapidly passing northeast in the sky, followed by a persistent trail of smoke. The weather was clear with a few high-altitude clouds. The observation lasted between one and two seconds. He deduced that it might have been a meteorite. No other reports were collected. The witness's impression of a meteorite was probably correct, but the description was too brief to confirm it. The description was not particularly unusual. Consequently, GEIPAN classified this case as Category C: lack of reliable information.

summary: Observations of the movement of luminous phenomena in the sky with changes of direction: lack of information.
description: witness contacted GEIPAN on March 31, 2009, regarding a sighting of a yellow sphere observed on Sunday, March 22, 2009, and another similar sighting on October 13, 2009. These two sightings were analyzed together by GEIPAN but processed in two separate files (see the investigation report). GEIPAN attempted to contact the witness again in 2012, but the phone number and email address provided in 2009 proved unusable in 2012. Apart from the changes in direction, the testimony strongly resembles the observation of an atmospheric reentry of satellite or meteoroid debris, or a festive lantern. This is a moderately unusual sighting, but the overall consistency does not allow for a D1 classification. This case is classified as C due to a lack of independent and corroborating witness statements.

summary: Black circles several meters in diameter of myxomycetes.
description: On the mornings of October 2nd, 3rd, and 5th, 2007, people found circles of black debris in their lawns. Appearing overnight, these circles ranged in diameter from 5.80 meters to 10 meters and were approximately 30 centimeters wide. During investigations conducted by the gendarmerie and GEIPAN (the French National Group for the Study and Protection of the Environment), samples were taken. Analysis of these samples, entrusted to the mycology department of the Toulouse Faculty of Pharmacy, led to the identification of an exceptional formation of Myxomycetes of the genus Badhamia, organisms related to fungi, intermediate between the animal and plant kingdoms.

summary: Sightings of a large shape flying slowly and silently in the sky: probable sightings of festive helium-filled balloons.
description: On October 2, 2007, around 1 p.m., a witness in his garden observed a peculiar phenomenon in the sky: a large, multicolored, diamond-shaped object flying silently at low altitude. Intrigued, the witness decided to follow the phenomenon by car for 5 to 6 km between Neuville-les-Dames and Vonnas. He took photographs during the chase and met four other witnesses in the parking lot of a horticultural company in Vonnas, who were also intrigued. The witness then continued driving towards Mezeriat but lost sight of the object. Following an appeal for witnesses published in the newspaper Le Progrès, numerous people came forward. The reconstruction of the trajectory, consistent with the observations, indicated a direction of movement from south-southwest to north-northeast, very close to that of the southerly wind recorded in Lyon. The object's average speed during the observation (20 km/h) was slightly lower than the wind speed (22 km/h). These two observations clearly point the investigation towards the hypothesis of a lighter-than-air aerostat, and therefore carried by the wind (see investigation report). The appearance described by witnesses suggests a cluster of small, festive Mylar balloons, inflated with helium. It may have escaped its owner, or conversely, it may have been assembled to carry a small payload. This cluster of balloons may have traveled a considerable distance before the observation, making it very difficult to determine its origin. This case of observation, with several witnesses and photographs, thus proves to be very consistent, but ultimately not very strange since the object's movement is consistent with the wind direction and speed. Following the investigation, GEIPAN classifies this case as B: probable observation of festive balloons inflated with helium.

summary: observation of eight white lights grouped four by four
description: On October 1, 2007, at 7:40 a.m., a motorist on the A27, 5.5 km from the Belgian border, observed a dark gray unidentified flying object (UFO) 1-2 km ahead of his vehicle. The object had a delta wing shape and a wingspan exceeding 100 meters. White lights were positioned on the rear edge of the wings. He continued driving for another 1-2 km, then pulled over onto the hard shoulder approximately 400 meters from the UFO. The object appeared to be hovering above a field at an altitude of about 100 meters. After about ten seconds, the unidentified flying object (UFO) tilted and then moved away at a speed of 30 to 40 km/h. Although the witness did not recognize an aircraft, the investigation initially focused on the possibility of an aircraft sighting because the approach path for aircraft at Lille-Lesquin Airport is located in a line close to the line of trees. Furthermore, during the reconstruction, an approaching aircraft was observed. Its apparent size was similar to that of the object seen by the witness, but the aircraft was positioned much higher above the trees. The second hypothesis put forward was that the witness had seen a Thalys train or a TGV train on the Lille-Brussels line. The TGV line is indeed visible from certain points along the highway. However, this hypothesis will be abandoned because, from the witness's location, the section of track where the train would have been at the time of the observation runs through a cutting: any observation is therefore impossible, even a few dozen meters from the track. At this stage of the investigation, and pending further inquiries, no explanation can be offered.

summary: Probable meteor strike.
description: On September 28, 2007, at 3:50 a.m., a moving point of light was observed during a regional flight. Traveling in the opposite direction to the aircraft, the brightness of the phenomenon gradually diminished. Too low to be a satellite, the crew likely witnessed a meteor shower.

summary: Astronomical observation of Venus.
description: On September 26, 2007, at 7:30 a.m., two people were intrigued by a luminous phenomenon in the cloudy sky. To the southeast, at an altitude of approximately 100 meters, an oval shape emitted a very dense light. This stationary shape slowly rose vertically starting at 9:15 a.m. and disappeared around 11:00 a.m. On September 27, 2007, one of the witnesses observed this shape again. It was later demonstrated that the witnesses had made an astronomical observation of Venus, which was particularly visible at that time of year (magnitude -4.31). These astronomical observations were confirmed by the September 2007 issue of the magazine Sciences et Vie.

summary: Observations of the movement of a white teche moving rapidly in the sky: probable observations from a scientific balloon.
description: On September 18, 2007, a motorist was intrigued by the sighting of an object in the sky. She called her husband, who also witnessed the rapid movement of a large, oval, white patch in the sky. According to the police investigation, no object fell to the ground in the area indicated. This observation is somewhat unusual: the object's shape and its movement with the wind (Mistral: N to NW) are characteristic of a balloon, which was very bright at the end of the day. It is possible that it was a scientific balloon launched by the Haute-Provence Observatory (this has not been verified). This case is classified as "B," indicating a probable observation of a scientific balloon.

summary: Probable observation of satellites passing overhead.
description: On September 13, 2007, between 5:08 and 5:13 AM, a witness observed two bright points of light (white with reddish reflections) outside their home, separated by approximately two degrees, passing north-south from their home. No noise was heard during the observation. The described observation largely corresponds to a satellite transit: a straight trajectory followed by gradual disappearance (extinction). At this time of day and season, many satellites pass along this trajectory. The two objects could be the satellite and its launch vehicle: it is noted that on September 11, 2007, the COSMOS 2429 launch vehicle launched the SL-8 R/B satellite into a near-polar orbit (the time of visibility could not be verified). The high brightness is, however, surprising: these objects should not be so bright (magnitude 4). The perception of immobility for 5 seconds at the beginning of the observation is not consistent with this hypothesis, but could be a perceptual error. Despite these uncertainties, this case is classified as "B": probable observation of satellites, due to the low strangeness of the phenomenon.

summary: Unexplained stain on a photo: probable passage of a bird or insect.
description: witness reported observing a strange shape in a photograph without having directly observed anything unusual during the shooting process. This type of case—spots appearing in a photo when nothing was visually apparent—has become very frequent with the proliferation of digital cameras. The origin of the larger spot is probably a bird or insect passing relatively close to the camera, hence the blur. The faint central gray spot is a slight camera defect, likely visible in all photos. This rather unusual case is classified as "B": probable passage of a bird or insect into the camera's field of view.

summary: Observation and video of the passage of a bright flash in the sky; descending curved trajectory: lack of information and cross-checking.
description: On Thursday, August 30, 2007, at approximately 7:00 PM, a witness, looking out of a window, was drawn to a star-like flash in the clear sky. He took out his camcorder to film it. The light intensity decreased, and the witness saw a small, dark object that became just a moving dark spot. Intrigued, the witness went into another room to follow the object, zoomed in with his camcorder, and saw four black dots or squares surrounding the flash. The observation lasted less than 25 seconds. Only one witness statement was recorded. The phenomenon observed by the witness was a very bright point of light, most likely a reflection of the sun on a flying object. The video of the phenomenon produced four black rectangles surrounding the white point: these elements are clearly artifacts, that is, unwanted effects of the video sensor and compression. The strangeness of this case is therefore reduced to the passage of a flying object reflecting the sun. The wind is blowing strongly today (Mistral) from the north to northwest (see Météociel). As the object's movement is from northeast to southwest, it is very unlikely to be a wind-borne object. However, an airplane or helicopter may have acted as a mirror to the sun, which is low on the horizon (due west, at 8°). The strong wind would have masked the aircraft's noise. The investigation was carried out too late to confirm this hypothesis. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of information and corroboration.

summary: Observations of a round, flat object moving from East to West.
description: On August 28, 2007, between 7:00 and 7:10 PM, two people observed a peculiar flying object from their terrace for three or four minutes. It was round, flat, and had a transparent dome. The object rose while swaying and moved from east to west. The underside of the object appeared dark. No noise was heard. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected. After investigation, it appears that the witnesses likely saw a Circoflex-type kite.

summary: Observation of the movement of a round object with 4 fins: probable observation of a helium-filled balloon.
description: witness sitting on a café terrace observed the slow, silent passage of a strangely spherical object with fins. It moved from east to west and rose vertically into the sky. The witness was unable to continue following the object, which then entered direct sunlight. No further witness accounts were collected. The object described by the witness did indeed resemble, as the witness stated, an inflatable advertising display. The witness reported a westerly wind felt at ground level, which contradicts this hypothesis, but weather reports from nearby Lille indicated an easterly wind, which would then be consistent with the object's movement. It can be assumed that the wind felt at ground level was very different from the wind at an altitude of 100 meters. The object's rotation and erratic movements are not surprising for an object of this shape flying with the wind. This case is class "B" probable observation of a helium-filled balloon, probably escaped from its owner.

summary: Observation of the movement of a point of light: passage of the ISS.
description: An amateur astronomer reported his observation of August 18, 2007: around 10:15 PM, while observing the stars, he noticed a bright point of light moving from east to west at a constant speed. After 30 seconds of observation, he decided to record a video with his camcorder. He first filmed at maximum zoom (20x) and then zoomed out to better follow the point of light. The witness was intrigued by this same phenomenon, which he saw two more times in August 2007. The witness observed a point of light that began to move, so he took out his camera and filmed it. The movements of the phenomenon on the witness's video (of very limited usability) correspond to the camera's movement; the diamond shape is the shape of the camera's aperture. It could be an airplane bound for Blagnac Airport, seen from the front, with its landing lights on, but the witness did not answer the additional questions asked for the investigation. After initially being classified as "C" due to a lack of information, this case has been re-examined. On August 18th at 10:15 PM, a pass of the International Space Station (ISS) was visible from Gimont. GEIPAN now classifies the case as "A": observation of the International Space Station (ISS).

summary: Probable atmospheric re-entry.
description: On the night of August 15, 2007, between 11:25 PM and 11:45 PM, a witness observed a peculiar phenomenon in the clear sky. A dark metallic gray object, surrounded by an orange halo and trails behind it, crossed the sky. During the six-second observation, the object moved from east to northwest. The object then suddenly disappeared. No sound was heard. The description and duration are consistent with what is typically seen during atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation by a motorist of a large luminous disc in the landscape: lack of information and cross-checking.
description: Recent report (2013) of an earlier observation (2007). On August 15, 2007, at 11:45 PM, a witness, while driving, observed a large luminous disk which he initially mistook for the Moon. The phenomenon was obscured by the landscape for a few minutes, after which the UFO was no longer visible. Astronomical verification confirmed that the Moon was indeed not visible at that time (slender crescent, set for over an hour). However, it was observed that the planet Jupiter was very close to the direction of observation indicated by the witness, and that it was particularly bright (magnitude -2). It is nonetheless surprising that it was perceived as large as the Moon. The Meteociel weather forecast indicated overcast skies with intermittent rain. This could be due to the scattering effect of low clouds creating a halo around Jupiter. (See a halo in winter). In a completely different vein, one could also consider the headlight of a farm vehicle on a ridge, seen through the mist after rain. It is very difficult, in retrospect, to confirm or refute either of these hypotheses. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of information and corroboration.

summary: observation of the passage of the international space station
description: On August 13, 2007, at approximately 11:30 PM, a family was stargazing from their garden. They observed a luminous phenomenon in the sky that intrigued them: a bright white sphere, coming from the west, grew larger as it moved toward them. Gradually changing its trajectory to head toward Polaris, the sphere diminished in size before disappearing completely. A star chart taken at the indicated times and locations shows that these people witnessed the passage of the International Space Station.

summary: curious image in a photo without visual observation: a bird taking flight at the moment the photo was taken.
description: While viewing his photographs on his computer, a person discovered a strange image in one of them. The photographs were taken from a distance of approximately 1800 meters with a powerful 100-300mm zoom lens and a teleconverter. After examining the series of photos, it became quite clear that it was a large bird taking flight at the moment the picture was taken. The shooting conditions (distance, zoom lens, and positioning inside a car) meant that the photographer didn't notice the bird, which hadn't yet flown away in the first photo and had completely disappeared in the third. This kind of oversight is particularly common, and we very regularly have to identify birds in photos that the photographer didn't notice. Seeing a bird fly by is so commonplace that the brain, focused on taking the picture, completely blocks out this information.

summary: stain on a photograph without visual observation during the shooting process.
description: On August 5, 2007, a very large hot air balloon event took place at the former military base of Chambley-Bussiere (54). Thousands of people attended, and thousands of photos were taken. After the event, one of the participants noticed a suspicious mark on one of his photos (approximately 190) that did not appear to be an aircraft, a bird, or any kind of camera artifact. He contacted a private investigator, Mr. Christian Comtesse, and GEIPAN (the French UFO investigation group) was only alerted by the media coverage of this event, which was dubbed the "Chambley UFO sighting." A case of observation consisting of a single photograph showing an anomaly, without any visual observation at the time the photograph was taken, makes any in-depth investigation difficult: the lack of precise information leads to numerous hypotheses, but without the possibility of verifying them, and if there are not at least two independent sources of information, the case of observation is of little interest a priori. Locally, Mr. Christian Comtesse, who had received only one photograph, undertook to try to learn more. He collected many other photographs, and the same spot is present in another photograph. In this particular case, one of the photographs collected during Christian Comtesse's investigation is relatively rich in information (presence of numerous balloons at varying distances). It served as the basis for a study of photographic analysis procedures entrusted to François Louange, a specialist in the field. The complete analysis of the photograph is detailed in an appendix (Louange Photo Analysis Report), and the conclusion is that it depicts an object between 75 cm and 1 meter in size, located approximately 300 meters from the photographer. A plausible hypothesis is that it was a child's balloon that had escaped. C. Comtesse's tenacity was rewarded when, in March 2008, he finally obtained the testimony of the pilot of one of the hot air balloons, an eyewitness to the object. This object turned out to be precisely a child's balloon in the shape of a fish, approximately 80 cm in diameter. Christian Comtesse's report, submitted to GEIPAN, is published in an appendix (Chambley UFO Investigation Report). This case, ultimately classified as Class A, is exemplary in more ways than one: - It demonstrates the value of collaboration between GEIPAN and local investigators, a collaboration now established by GEIPAN with First-Level Responders (FIRST-LEVEL Responders): indeed, without Christian Comtesse's collaboration, this case of a photograph taken without visual observation would not have been thoroughly investigated by GEIPAN and would therefore perhaps remain unexplained (and probably Class C). - It validates, in retrospect, the method of photograph analysis developed by François Louange for GEIPAN.

summary: Probable sighting of a balloon.
description: On August 4, 2007, around 2 PM, a family observed a small, bright sphere moving at varying speeds and changing direction. The level of strangeness of the observation is low: a large proportion of the described characteristics of the phenomenon correspond to those of known phenomena (balloons). The proposed interpretation is plausible for explaining the observation. Although based on a single testimony (a questionnaire without a police report), the quantity and quality of the information describing the observation are objective and reliable. The case is classified as Class B, meaning the observation of a balloon is highly probable.

summary: A quick observation of a luminous green ball. No sound.
description: On the night of August 2, 2007, around 1:00 AM, two witnesses observed a luminous green sphere moving. Spiraling downwards, the object disappeared from their sight behind a hangar. No noise was heard during the observation. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected in the area. The IPN investigation was unsuccessful due to a lack of contact with the witness. The characteristics of the observation suggest an uncatalogued meteor (duration = 2 seconds, green sphere), but any investigation is impossible due to the lack of contact and therefore information.

summary: Observation of two yellow spheres in motion.
description: On August 8, 2008, a witness contacted GEIPAN by telephone to describe a previous sighting. Sometime after August 15, 2007 (the witness no longer remembered the exact date), and between 10:30 PM and 11:00 PM, this person saw two bright yellow luminous spheres moving side by side in a southeasterly direction. No further information regarding this sighting could be gathered.

summary: Observation in the sky of a colored object rotating on its axis.
description: Recent report (August 30, 2010) of a previous sighting (August 2007; the witness does not recall the exact date). A witness reports that in August 2007, on a beach, they observed a bright object with very vividly colored facets behind an advertising plane. The object was stationary but appeared to rotate very slowly. No sound was heard. The sighting lasted two or three minutes before the object disappeared. No further reports were collected on this phenomenon, for which we lack details and information.

summary: Probable sighting of a balloon.
description: In May 2008, a witness reported that on July 29, 2007, around 8:00 PM, he and several other people observed a dark-colored sphere with irregular light patches passing across the sky. This sphere, with a protrusion at its front, moved in a straight line along a west-southeast trajectory. During the observation, which lasted about thirty seconds, no noise was heard and no smoke was noticed. These people likely saw a balloon; however, no hypothesis can be verified given the time elapsed since the observation.

summary: Observing two satellites simultaneously.
description: On July 27, 2007, between 11:30 PM and 12:15 AM, a witness sitting on a café terrace curiously observed a bright point of light moving rapidly at a very high altitude in the sky. This point, moving south, had a descending trajectory. While discussing the observation with a friend, she resumed watching but realized the object was now in the opposite direction and on an ascending trajectory. Examination of a star chart showed that, around midnight that day, the International Space Station disappeared below the horizon a few seconds before the NOAA 14 weather satellite rose in the exact same position in the sky, in the direction of the observation. The trajectories of these two satellites are approximately 90°. The ISS rose from the southwest (204°) at 11:45 PM on that date, heading southeast. The NOAA-14 weather satellite rose in the exact same position (204th) at 0:03 AM and moved in the opposite direction towards the SW. It is therefore clear that the witness saw the ISS and then NOAA 14 successively, which gave him the impression that the point of light was changing direction.

summary: Probable observation of the nighttime passage of an aircraft, airplane type.
description: On July 18, 2007, at approximately 4:45 a.m., a witness observed a curious luminous phenomenon from their terrace. A light moved, approached, then changed direction and disappeared. The witness heard no noise during the observation. The data provided by the witness regarding the location of the observation did not allow for the identification of a precise point, but rather an area (based on the distances to neighboring villages estimated by the witness). The observation of a growing light approaching the witness corresponded to the front landing light of an aircraft approaching Figari Airport. The absence of noise was due to the wind direction, coming from the East-Northeast, behind the witness.

summary: Observation of a plot on onboard radar: probable false echoes.
description: On July 14, 2007, at 2:35 PM UTC, the captain of an Air France flight reported a T-CAS alert indicating traffic very close to the aircraft. On the screens, the pilots saw a red marker located 30 nautical miles (55 km) and 300 feet (100 m) above the aircraft. However, no object was seen by the pilots despite exceptional visibility. Air traffic control detected no unknown traffic on the radar screen. The preliminary investigation conducted by the Bureau of Investigation and Analysis at Le Bourget for the French Civil Aviation Authority (DGAC) concluded that the observed phenomenon was due to false echoes. The expert analysis carried out for GEIPAN (French Interministerial Group for the Study of Aeronautical and Nuclear Events) highlighted a probable malfunction of an onboard instrument: the Active Traffic Alert and Collision Avoidance System (T-CAS).

summary: Observation of a triangular aerial phenomenon.
description: Observation made by two witnesses of a triangular aerial phenomenon seen for one minute above Bourges on the night of July 12-13, 2007. The witnesses did not wish to make a statement, making any investigation impossible due to lack of information.

summary: Spots on photos: bird traffic.
description: A witness later discovered unexplained artifacts in some wedding photos. He filed a report with the St. Germain-en-Laye police station, handing over the photographs. Having no prior visual observation of the phenomenon, analysis of the three photos clearly showed that the black dots corresponded to birds flying in the frame.

summary: Recent testimony of an old observation of a green incandescent spherical luminous phenomenon with random movements in the air: strong hypothesis of globular lightning but lack of information.
description: Recent testimony (2016) of an earlier observation (July 2007). On July 7, 2007, around 3:00 a.m., a motorist and his friend traveling on the N118 highway in the Bordeaux-Nantes direction were surprised to see a luminous phenomenon, spherical in shape and incandescent green with a light greenish halo, moving randomly through the air with frequent changes of direction. The observation, at close range, lasted about twenty seconds before the UFO disappeared. The witness initially thought it might be ball lightning but dismissed this hypothesis due to the absence of stormy weather. He emphasized the proximity of the CEA Saclay research center. Only one witness statement was collected. According to the expert consulted, the observation, in terms of the phenomenon's behavior, duration, and color, is consistent with a case of ball lightning. However, the testimony is late (11 years after the observation) and therefore does not allow access to meteorological data (including storm conditions?) that could support this hypothesis. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C (due to its proximity to a B case: ball lightning).

summary: Observation of the silent movements of a vaporous white-blue luminous phenomenon in the cloudy sky: mistaken for the projections of a sky tracer (laser projector).
description: On July 6, 2007, at approximately 1:00 AM, a motorist and his wife witnessed a hazy, bluish-white luminous phenomenon in the shape of an oval ring, moving silently and slightly tilted across the cloudy sky. Outside the ring, the witnesses also saw several luminous circles. The phenomenon appeared to follow the vehicle, which frightened the witnesses, between the Remiremont (88) exit and Dinoze (88). Upon arriving home, the witnesses continued to observe the phenomenon. The intermittent observation lasted approximately 35 minutes over a distance of just over 20 kilometers. The appearance of the UFO described by the witnesses closely resembles images projected onto the base of clouds by a sky tracer (multi-beam laser projector). The investigation demonstrated (see the investigation report) that, firstly, the Epinal nightclub possessed such equipment at the time of the sighting, and secondly, that the visibility and behavior of the UFO are consistent with witness accounts. Furthermore, in 2007, the laser projector was in operation on Thursdays in addition to Friday and Saturday nights. In 2015, it is still possible to verify the explanatory hypothesis on Thursday, Friday, and Saturday nights, starting at 11:00 PM in cloudy weather. It is thanks in particular to the quality of the witnesses' recollections and the notes taken at the time of the events by the witness, as well as the meticulous reconstruction carried out by the investigators, that this case can be classified as A: mistaken identity involving a sky tracer (laser projector).

summary: Observation of a weather balloon.
description: On the morning of June 30, 2007, a witness observed an intriguing object in the sky. Upon returning home, he filmed the object, which was still present. The video clearly shows that the observed object was a torahedral balloon, of the type used by the National Meteorological Service or scientists.

summary: Observation of a weather balloon.
description: Following a documentary viewed online, a witness reported to us in November 2008 concerning an observation made on June 30, 2007. A motorist driving on the A410 motorway towards Annecy observed an object suspended in the air at 9:43 AM. Dark in color and multifaceted, the object moved very slowly, oscillating. A photograph was taken while driving with a mobile phone; according to the witness, it did not accurately depict the color and shape of the observed object. By comparing this observation with another case (Annemasse (74), also on the same date but late morning), the witness was able to formally identify the object as a torahedral weather balloon used by the French National Weather Service (Météo Nationale) or scientists.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a very bright luminous phenomenon in the sky: passage of the ISS and the shuttle.
description: A person reported an observation made on June 19, 2007, at 10:10 PM. From their balcony, the witness's attention was drawn to the silent north-south passage of a very bright object, closely followed by a second, much larger object. The entire system moved at a constant speed and disappeared behind a hill on a downward trajectory. No other reports were collected about this phenomenon. A pass of the International Space Station (ISS), accompanied by the space shuttle that had just undocked from the station, occurred that same day within sight of Nyons. This event is classified as Class A, as is the observation of an ISS and shuttle pass.

summary: Probable sighting of a Transall type aircraft
description: On June 12, 2007, at approximately 10:30 PM, two witnesses at home heard a deafening noise for 10 minutes but saw nothing through their windows. At precisely 12:08 AM, the same rumbling sound was heard again, and one of the witnesses saw a gray, triangular object with colored lights for about five seconds. The object was flying at a very low altitude in a specific direction. It disappeared from the witness's sight, and the noise gradually faded away. Several Transall aircraft had flown in the area during the night of June 12-13, and the witness's description supported the hypothesis of a possible aircraft sighting.

summary: Observing Jupiter.
description: On June 9, 2007, at approximately 1:30 a.m., a witness observed a very bright light in the sky, which intrigued him. He filmed the phenomenon for several minutes. As the Nice East gendarmerie was very reluctant to take his statement, he contacted GEIPAN directly. His testimony was therefore recorded on a direct questionnaire and not in a police report. A search using the Winstars 2 software quickly showed that the witness had observed Jupiter under very favorable conditions, which were also mentioned in the June issue of Sciences et Avenir magazine. The witness himself, who conducted his own analysis, reached the same conclusion. The phenomenon was therefore definitively identified.

summary: Bright spots on night photos: lack of information.
description: On May 12, 2007, two witnesses taking photos at the Col de Vence observed spots on their pictures without any visual evidence. This type of photo is unusable and no serious analysis can be carried out.

summary: Observation of the movements of a low-altitude flying object.
description: In March 2009, a witness reported an earlier sighting. On April 24, 2007, between 10 p.m. and midnight, a motorist on a country road observed and followed a low-flying object that intrigued him. No other witness statements were collected. The observed object resembled a reconnaissance helicopter: its speed and movements were consistent with those of a helicopter. The perceived noise was faint, but the witness was in his car. However, GEIPAN (the French National Gendarmerie Intervention Group) was unable to confirm this hypothesis due to the time elapsed between the sighting and the investigation. This case is classified as "C" due to a lack of evidence to validate the hypothesis.

summary: Observation for a few seconds of a triangle of three bright points moving at high speed
description: On Saturday, April 21, 2007, a person left their friends' house around 12:15 a.m. to go home. As they crossed the garden, they spotted three bright points of light forming a triangle in the sky directly above them. Calling their friends, they all went to see the triangle, which was moving silently at high speed. During the observation, which lasted less than 10 seconds, they saw faint orange lights at each end of the triangle. The object was moving from west to east. No further information was gathered about this phenomenon, for which we lack data.

summary: Observations of spots on photos during a regatta
description: On April 20, 2007, a witness took photos of a regatta taking place in the Brest harbor. Afterward, he noticed unexplained spots on some of the photos. Since he didn't see anything at the time the photos were taken, analyzing these types of photographs is very difficult. Furthermore, the images themselves are not very informative, and no other witness reported seeing anything similar that same day in the same location. Given that the Brest harbor is known for its many birds, it is highly likely that this witness photographed birds that went unnoticed when the photos were taken.

summary: Sirius observation
description: For several nights starting on April 15, 2007, at a campsite in Le Croisic (44), several witnesses observed a bright point in the sky. The phenomenon appeared as a large, luminous sphere with numerous color changes—green, red, and blue—observed through binoculars. During the investigation, the police officers themselves witnessed the phenomenon and took a series of photographs as well as a video sequence of approximately 13 seconds. The preliminary analysis was entrusted to an expert astronomer who quickly leaned towards the hypothesis of an astronomical phenomenon, as the sky was particularly clear during this period and conducive to spectacular observations. To support this hypothesis, a field investigation was conducted from June 11 to 13, 2007: it was demonstrated that the witnesses had observed Sirius, a star particularly visible at this time of year. Several calls to GEIPAN during the same period reported seeing particularly bright stars. The investigation also served as the basis for the filming of the program "Pieces à convictions" on June 29th on France 3.

summary: Observation of an aircraft passing overhead.
description: During the night of March 30-31, 2007, between 8:00 PM and 2:00 AM near Dompaire (88), four young witnesses repeatedly observed white and red lights in the dark, stormy sky. These lights formed a metallic triangle that moved back and forth at varying speeds before passing approximately 15 to 20 meters above their vehicle. This observation ended around 2:00 AM. The witnesses were deeply impressed by this experience. During the investigation, an analysis of air traffic in the area indicated the landing of a cargo plane in Epinal at 1:58 a.m. and confirmed a crew training exercise for an MD 90 (DC9) belonging to the Swiss company Hello AG during the hours observed by witnesses: the aircraft, arriving from Zurich, performed 30 touch-and-go maneuvers around the Epinal runway in the afternoon after detecting a technical problem, then resumed these same maneuvers between 7:47 p.m. and 9:16 p.m.; the final takeoff for Zurich occurred at 9:45 p.m. This type of training is common on runways with low traffic, and Hello AG is a frequent user of the Epinal runway. It is likely that, given the state of mind of the witnesses, the bright spot observed around 2 a.m. was mistaken for a streetlamp or car light, as had happened several times during their travels, as they themselves explained. There is no doubt that the observation made by the group of friends was of the DC-9 of the Hello AG airline during training exercises: the witnesses were always directly under the aircraft's flight path, which was observed in unusual conditions around the Epinal-Mirecourt airport.

summary: Observation of a luminous phenomenon in the Parisian sky: lack of information.
description: On Friday, February 29, 2008, GEIPAN received an email accompanied by two photographs showing a luminous sphere, corresponding to an observation of a luminous phenomenon in the sky made on the evening of March 26, 2007. This testimony is rather weak: the account was given several months after the event, it is somewhat confused, unreliable although certainly sincere; the long-exposure photograph is difficult to interpret (doubt remains about the camera shake: was it due to the object or the camera?). The observed phenomenon is not very strange: it is only a point of light whose movement is poorly characterized, both by the witness and by the photograph; the change in shape is rather strange but could be due to a change in position. Given these various inaccuracies, this case is classified as C due to a lack of reliable information.

summary: Observation after the fact on photographs of a black dot without direct observation when the photos were taken: photographic artifact.
description: On January 21, 2007, a witness took several photographs during an early afternoon walk. Upon developing the photos, the witness noticed black dots that reappeared in the center of the sun. The witness saw nothing unusual while taking the pictures. Following a television program in 2008, the witness sent us the questionnaire and the photos. This case is a typical example of an anomaly arising from the interpretation of a photo or video and not perceived by the witness in real time with their own eyes. GEIPAN no longer processes these reports because experience shows that, with sometimes considerable effort, explanations can be found through artifacts resulting from the operation of the device. These artifacts are varied and more frequent due to the now widespread use of smartphones. Some cases, like this one, are nevertheless processed and published for informational purposes. This particular case illustrates a black sun phenomenon. This occurs when a camera is pointed at a scene containing a highly concentrated light source, such as the sun's disk. (Note: This is not recommended for prolonged use with any digital camera, as the image of the sun's disk on a sensor can cause irreparable damage to both the sensor and the lens.) Under these conditions, one might expect the resulting image to be uniformly saturated and therefore white, whether of the sun's disk or any other bright object in the scene. However, some sensors (mostly CMOS) actually render these ultra-bright areas as black, rather than saturated, as particularly evident in photos 78 and 82 of the sample. The link IPACO Expert Report provides a more precise description of the technological phenomenon. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: photographic artifact.

summary: Passage of 3 objects with a trail of smoke.
description: On January 9, 2007, a witness observed three objects emitting smoke passing by. Too little information was available for a serious analysis.

summary: Quick observation of a large metallic shape in the sky.
description: A brief, recent account (March 28, 2010) of a past observation (the date given is arbitrary). In the spring of 2007 (early May, according to the witness who did not provide a precise date), two people were startled by a fleeting glimpse of a large mass in the sky. It was 11:30 PM, and there was heavy fog in the residential area. While returning to their car on the street, the two witnesses twice observed, at a distance and altitude of approximately 500 meters, an enormous, motionless metallic shape surrounded by a halo of light. No sound was heard during these very brief observations. No other accounts of this phenomenon were collected. Any investigation is impossible due to a lack of sufficient information.
